title: Avoid quadratic list copying in the autologging metrics queue
body:
### Related Issues/PRs No linked issue. ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? Preparing a queued metrics flush performs repeated list copying twice: grouping a run's metrics concatenates an ever-growing list, and removing each snapshot item repeatedly shifts the queue's remaining elements. These costs grow quadratically when a busy background logger accumulates a large queue. Append metrics to each run's list and delete the captured queue prefix in one operation. Producers only append; the flush lock excludes other removals. Deleting exactly the captured prefix therefore preserves metrics appended after the snapshot. Run order, per-run metric order, duplicates, and the queue object's identity are retained. A local benchmark times the complete `flush_metrics_queue` call with `MlflowClient` mocked to exclude network and storage work. Five repetitions per size produced these median CPU times: | Queued metrics | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | 500 (normal flush threshold) | 0.288 ms | 0.137 ms | | 10,000 (backlog) | 55.594 ms | 0.469 ms | | 50,000 (backlog) | 1,690.063 ms | 1.871 ms | These measurements isolate queue preparation on one machine; they are not end-to-end training or server benchmarks. The larger rows characterize backlog handling, not the usual 500-item queue. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [x] Manual tests `pytest -p pytest_mock -p pytest_timeout tests/utils/test_metrics_queue.py tests/utils/test_autologging_utils.py -q`: 10 passed. The seven new controls cover empty and large grouping, object identity/order, duplicate entries, and metrics appended by another thread while a flush is logging. All ten also pass on the baseline; this is a performance change with behavior-preservation checks. Pinned Ruff, Clint, character normalization, and `git diff --check` pass. The complete repository suite was not run. Full pre-commit initialization is blocked in this environment by npm's `EALLOWGIT` restriction on the Prettier environment; Python checks were run directly. The timing loop prepares `[("run", Metric("loss", float(i), 0, i)) for i in range(size)]`, replaces the queue contents before each repetition, patches `metrics_queue.MlflowClient`, times `flush_metrics_queue()` with `perf_counter`, and verifies that the mocked batch contains all `size` metrics. ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] Yes. Reduce CPU overhead when autologging flushes a backlog of queued training metrics. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? Components - [x] `area/tracking`: Tracking Service, tracking client APIs, autologging #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [x] `rn/bug-fix` - A user-facing bug fix worth mentioning in the release notes #### Is this PR a critical bugfix or security fix that should go into the next patch release?
What is a minor/patch release? - Minor release: a release that increments the second part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0). Minor releases are expected to contain larger changes, such as new features and improvements. Non-critical bug fixes and doc updates can be included as well. By default, your PR should target the next minor release. - Patch release: a release that increments the third part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.2.1). Patch releases are typically only performed when there has been a major regression or bug in the latest release. For the sake of stability, your PR should not be included in a patch release unless it is a critical fix, or if the risk level of your PR is exceedingly low.
- [ ] This PR is critical and needs to be in the next patch release - [x] This PR can wait for the next minor release
